problem: Navigation instruction generation (NIG) has been treated as trajectory captioning / auxiliary VLN data augmentation, requiring the route to be given; endpoint-only methods (GoViG) hallucinate over long distances. Generating goal-oriented instructions from compact video priors, where the route is not simply the tour, remains unexplored and hard for MLLMs.
motivation: VLN agents need fine-grained instructions that are burdensome for users to write, whereas users would prefer to give only a goal. Ego-centric tour videos are a compact, dense, video-native prior in persistent environments, avoiding explicit maps/graphs. Existing MLLMs have improved spatial abilities on benchmarks but perform poorly here, showing semantic fragmentation over long videos.
key_idea: Define VideoNIG (generate executable navigation instructions from an ego-centric tour video, initial observation, and a text or image goal) and train MLLMs with a two-stage curriculum (Action Warmup, then Complexity Progression over increasingly exploratory tours).
insight: Curriculum ablation shows both stages matter: with neither stage, average Multiple/Orthogonal-choice is 48.33/52.29; with both, 56.73/62.92, and the warmup alone gives only small gains. Choice Evaluation correlates far more strongly with downstream VLN SR than Rouge-L/SPICE, so text overlap is a weak proxy for instruction quality. GRPO tuned on Rouge/SPICE gets the best text scores but weaker choice and execution results than MPO with spatial negatives; performance drops steadily from Gold Route to Explorer tours.
method: Task definition: model P(I | goal G, initial RGB O0, tour video V) where the tour covers the optimal route and may include extra observations; goals are text or image.

Benchmark construction: 60K tour videos rendered in Habitat from R2R-CE/RxR-CE (Gold Route, Tyro, Curiosity, Explorer tours with graded offsets, look-arounds and neighbourhood visits), filtered by nDTW<0.8, outlier ensembles (Z-score/RANSAC/Isolation Forest) and discriminability checks; 37K goal descriptions captioned by qwen3-vl-plus.

Diagnostic evaluation: Rouge-L/SPICE, Multiple-choice (5 distractor types: direction/entity change, subpath delete/add/change/swap), Orthogonal-choice (direction and entity only), and navigation execution with InternVLA-N1 (System2 / DualVLN).
Stage 1 Action Warmup: GRPO on Qwen3-VL-8B with action-from-view and view-from-action tasks over 13 discrete actions, using hierarchical step rewards.

Stage 2 Complexity Progression: train from Gold Route/Tyro to Curiosity/Explorer tours with SFT on a mixed data recipe, then GRPO (reward: SPICE 0.1, Rouge-L 0.1, LLM-judge quality 0.2, MLLM trajectory consistency 0.6, length penalty) or MPO (SFT + preference loss against 5 negative types, then LoRA fine-tuning).
Chain-of-thought prompt: model first analyzes the current state and surroundings before generating instructions.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (fine-tuned with SFT/GRPO/MPO); execution via InternVLA-N1 (frozen VLN agent)
setting.training_data: VideoNIG train split (~17K Gold Route, ~50K tour videos) plus Action Warmup triplets from Habitat, mixed ~1:1 with text (math/code) and general multimodal data (RoomTour3D, SpaceR, ALLaVA, CogVLM)
setting.observation: Monocular ego-centric RGB tour video (6 fps, max 210 frames) plus initial RGB view and goal image/text
setting.action_space: Text output (instructions); the downstream VLN agent uses discrete Habitat actions
setting.privileged: Tour videos rendered from GT route waypoints in simulator serve as the environmental prior; GRPO training uses GT instructions and Gold Route video

numbers.extra: Averaged over 4 video types x R2R/RxR x image/text goals

numbers_note: VideoNIG is a new benchmark; tables are on filtered R2R-CE/RxR-CE val-unseen. Execution tables report many more variants (Tyro/Curiosity/Explorer tours). Table 1 values come from averages over 16 configurations; API models were evaluated on 100 sampled instances per config.
results: Curriculum-trained Qwen3-VL-8B beats the base model on all metrics: MPO-lora reaches average Multiple/Orthogonal-choice 60.62/61.97 vs 51.06/52.13, and GRPO reaches SPICE 0.192 vs 0.107. With a Gold Route, MPO instructions give SR 60.3 (R2R) with DualVLN vs 41.6 for base Qwen3-VL-8B, approaching GT instructions (63.4), but SR falls to about 20 on Explorer tours.
limitations: Simulator-only, indoor, controlled benchmark built from R2R-CE/RxR-CE with rendered tours; no naturally collected tour videos or real robot.
Performance degrades strongly with tour complexity (Explorer SR ~20 R2R, ~11 RxR), and generated instructions lag GT instructions due to style shift for the follower.
GRPO rewards rely on LLM/MLLM judges and text metrics; proprietary model evaluation uses only 100 samples per configuration.
